hirebotics.title: Hirebotics adds line tracking and linear rails to extend cobot capabilities
hirebotics.summary: New features help cobots paint moving parts and reach larger workpieces, bringing more flexibility to production lines.

sections.heading: Moving parts and larger workpieces
paragraphs: Hirebotics introduced line tracking for conveyor-based painting and a modular linear rail at IMTS 2026 in Chicago. Both use the Beacon platform as their main interface, extending the range of tasks its cobots can handle.

sections.heading: Painting without stopping the conveyor
paragraphs: Sensors detect the workpiece and an encoder tracks conveyor movement. The system adjusts the painting path as the part moves. Operators teach the direction and configure the task in Beacon; the company says conventional programming is not required.

sections.heading: Extending the working envelope
paragraphs: The cobot has a reach of about 1.75 metres. Rail sections add roughly 1.5 metres at a time, with custom lengths also available. This can help with long structures or difficult-to-move parts in welding, plasma cutting and painting applications.

sections.heading: Available features and future plans
paragraphs: At the time of publication, operators repositioned the rail manually. Hirebotics planned to add position confirmation in Beacon and targeted automatic rail movement for late 2026. Those planned capabilities should be distinguished from features already available.

locus.title: Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest win supply-chain robotics award
locus.summary: A deployment across three distribution centres has supported more than 13.2 million picks, with the companies reporting productivity gains and payback within a year.

sections.heading: Recognition for a working warehouse deployment
paragraphs: Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest received the Best Use of Robotics award at the 2026 Supply Chain Excellence Awards USA. The project started in Columbus in January 2024 and expanded to three sites within 14 months without major changes to existing shelving.

sections.heading: A fleet of more than 100 robots
paragraphs: Autonomous mobile robots support picking and putaway at distribution centres in Ohio, Texas and Nevada. According to the companies, the deployment has supported more than 13.2 million robot-assisted picks and approximately one million putaway transactions.

sections.heading: Productivity and payback
paragraphs: Picking rates rose from around 110 to more than 160 lines per hour, while putaway increased from about 30 to 91–96 lines per hour. The companies report payback within a year, shorter employee training and less reliance on temporary labour.

sections.heading: Moving staff between changing priorities
paragraphs: Using the same platform for both picking and putaway allows staff to move between tasks as demand changes. The aim is to support growth while maintaining the promise to ship orders received before 4 p.m. on the same day.

abz.title: ABZ Innovation opens a larger European drone factory
abz.summary: The new Szentendre facility in Hungary expands manufacturing for agricultural spraying, industrial cleaning and transport drones.

sections.heading: A new manufacturing base in Hungary
paragraphs: ABZ Innovation opened a facility in Szentendre around four times the size of its previous factory. The company aims to triple output in 2026 and double it again in 2027 as it responds to commercial drone demand.

sections.heading: Four product families
paragraphs: The range comprises L-Series spraying drones, S-Series seed and granular-material spreaders, C-Series high-pressure cleaning drones and M-Series multipurpose transport drones. The company reports deployments in more than 40 countries across six continents.

sections.heading: Production and after-sales support
paragraphs: The facility is intended to serve as a global manufacturing hub. ABZ emphasises European production, data control, training, spare parts and after-sales service for customers who use drones in their day-to-day operations.

sections.heading: The expansion behind the announcement
paragraphs: The investment follows a €7 million funding round in January 2026. ABZ says industrial cleaning is its fastest-growing product line. Its production targets remain plans whose eventual delivery will need to be assessed.

light.title: Control ambient light before tuning a robotic inspection camera
light.summary: Windows, overhead fixtures and nearby work areas can change inspection images. The lighting environment needs attention before camera settings are finalised.

sections.heading: External light makes images inconsistent
paragraphs: EVST recommends checking windows, overhead lighting and adjacent work areas before adjusting an inspection camera. Light that changes during the day can make settings that work at one time unreliable at another.

sections.heading: Start with the real inspection cell
paragraphs: The accompanying video shows a part inside a cell with transparent panels and a window behind it, while a local light moves with the end device. This illustrates the layout but does not establish image quality or defect-detection accuracy.

sections.heading: Match light control to its source
paragraphs: The article discusses panels or enclosures, short light pulses and optical filters. Each measure should be linked to the source it addresses, including reflections from guarding and the workpiece itself.

sections.heading: Test under changing conditions
paragraphs: When a light or camera moves with the robot, shielding effectiveness can vary with position. Images need to be checked at times with different levels of interfering light before the inspection view can be treated as reliable.

a3.title: A3 adds the business case for automation to its robotics course
a3.summary: A new investment-assessment module helps learners decide where industrial robotics can create value and how to evaluate a project.

sections.heading: Connecting robotics with business decisions
paragraphs: The Association for Advancing Automation, or A3, added a business-case module to its Introduction to Industrial Robotics course. It is intended to help learners identify where automation is appropriate and assess the value of a proposed investment.

sections.heading: Designed for newcomers
paragraphs: The self-paced course does not require a technical background. It is aimed at people entering the field, operations staff and others involved in business decisions about deploying robotics.

sections.heading: Looking beyond the robot purchase price
paragraphs: The new material covers project costs, returns and payback periods, opportunities to improve productivity and quality, and workforce implications. It also addresses early project planning, requests for proposals and selecting an integrator.

sections.heading: Applying the ideas to a real project
paragraphs: Learners can use A3’s Robot System Value Calculator to assess a system they are considering. The central idea is to begin with the problem that needs solving and then examine how technology could deliver a return.

digit.title: From Cassie to Digit 5: Agility Robotics’ path to workplace robots
digit.summary: Agility’s robot generations trace a shift from bipedal locomotion research to practical warehouse work, safety and production readiness.

sections.heading: From walking research to useful work
paragraphs: Agility Robotics began with Cassie, which took its first steps in 2016 and focused on bipedal movement. The first Digit followed in 2017 for researchers. The development path reflects a shift from walking performance to tasks that businesses need done.

sections.heading: Digit reaches commercial applications
paragraphs: Digit 3 in 2019 targeted package delivery and box handling, with a lifting capacity of about 18 kilograms. Ford bought the first two robots to explore deliveries from a vehicle to a doorstep. Digit 4, introduced in 2023, focused on warehouses and distribution centres.

sections.heading: Workplace lessons inform Digit 5
paragraphs: The fifth generation changes the leg structure to favour force over speed and updates the battery and systems for operating near people. According to Agility, the robot assesses risk and slows down or stops when a person approaches.

sections.heading: Company scale and plans
paragraphs: The report describes a workforce of more than 400 and a factory capable of producing up to 10,000 robots per year. That figure is capacity, not actual deliveries. It also discusses a proposed SPAC transaction that had not been completed at the time of reporting.

gen7.title: Universal Robots introduces its AI-ready Gen 7 platform
gen7.summary: The new generation combines PolyScope X, updated robot arms, controllers and teaching interfaces for industrial automation.

sections.heading: A platform-wide update
paragraphs: Universal Robots introduced its seventh-generation platform at IMTS, with PolyScope X at its core. The update spans the controller, teach pendant and tool connections to support industrial applications that use AI.

sections.heading: New arms and controller hardware
paragraphs: The g-Series includes UR10g-1750, UR17g-1300 and UR18g-950 arms, with the names indicating payload and reach. Universal Robots says its CB7 Core controller provides 40% more processing power in a package 30% smaller, with support for multiple factory networks.

sections.heading: Connections for vision and AI
paragraphs: The tool flange provides data, power and connections needed for cameras and sensors. Force and torque sensing, APIs and ROS2 communication are intended to help integrators develop additional applications.

sections.heading: Making teaching easier
paragraphs: The TP7 Core pendant is more than 20% lighter, while the SP7 Smart Panel supports teaching close to the task. More than 20 partners contributed demonstrations. Users still need to select hardware and software suited to each application.

perciva.title: Teledyne e2v adds Perciva ToF to its 3D imaging range
perciva.summary: The new industrial depth camera combines a Hydra3D+ sensor and onboard processing for robotics, logistics and inspection.

sections.heading: Industrial depth sensing
paragraphs: Teledyne e2v introduced Perciva ToF for applications that need depth information, including logistics, robotics and inspection. The camera brings the sensor and processing together in a single device.

sections.heading: The Hydra3D+ sensor
paragraphs: Perciva uses an 832 × 600-pixel Hydra3D+ CMOS sensor with HiRho technology. The manufacturer says its pixel design supports near-infrared sensitivity and low-reflectivity materials while reducing imaging problems with fast-moving objects.

sections.heading: Ready-to-use data over GigE
paragraphs: Factory calibration and onboard processing allow the camera to deliver depth maps and 3D point clouds directly over GigE. This is intended to simplify integration for developers and system integrators.

sections.heading: Demonstrations and supporting information
paragraphs: The announcement says Teledyne plans to demonstrate the camera at VISION in Stuttgart on 6–8 October 2026 and offers documentation or product samples on request. The performance statements are manufacturer claims rather than independent tests in this report.

coating.title: Define coating requirements before configuring a painting robot
coating.summary: Corners, recesses, rear surfaces and suspension points need explicit requirements before a robot’s spray path can be assessed.

sections.heading: Specify each surface region
paragraphs: EVST recommends separate coating requirements for broad surfaces, corners, recesses, rear faces and hanging points. A single description of the desired finish for the whole part can leave important areas undefined.

sections.heading: Motion footage does not prove coating quality
paragraphs: The video shows a robot approaching a suspended part, but cannot establish film thickness or coverage outside the camera’s view. Contact points with the hanging fixture may have different permitted exceptions for different products.

sections.heading: Separate general principles from actual settings
paragraphs: Spray angle and nozzle distance affect coverage, but example settings from other spraying methods should not be transferred directly to a robot. The installed nozzle and actual system must be considered.

sections.heading: Test the unresolved requirement
paragraphs: If the question concerns a deep recess, a front-face inspection will not answer it. Tests need to match the location under review and the real hanging orientation. Validating the robot path and assessing coating quality are separate steps.

softbank.title: SoftBank agrees to acquire the Robotics and AI Institute
softbank.summary: The reported agreement would bring Marc Raibert’s research institute into SoftBank’s robotics portfolio, subject to review.

sections.heading: An agreement still under review
paragraphs: The Robot Report says SoftBank agreed to buy the Robotics and AI Institute from Hyundai. Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction was undergoing CFIUS review, with the precise review status unclear at the time of reporting.

sections.heading: Marc Raibert’s research institute
paragraphs: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, RAI was founded in 2022 with more than $400 million in initial investment from Hyundai. Its work spans control, perception, manipulation, navigation and AI for physical tasks.

sections.heading: An existing relationship in robotics
paragraphs: Marc Raibert founded both Boston Dynamics and RAI. SoftBank owned Boston Dynamics from 2017 to 2021 before Hyundai acquired a controlling stake, connecting the organisations through a longer history in robotics.

sections.heading: Questions that remain open
paragraphs: Raibert’s role after a completed deal was unclear. The report suggests RAI’s research could complement SoftBank’s robotics and AI portfolio, but the outcome still depends on approval and subsequent implementation.

sections.heading: A weekly collection of robotics videos
paragraphs: IEEE Spectrum’s Video Friday gathers demonstrations from multiple research and development teams. A highlight is a pair of connected two-propeller flying robots from CLIMB Lab, alongside developments in humanoids and automation.

sections.heading: Movement and working near people
paragraphs: The collection includes Digit 5 and work from Figure, as well as NYU’s WorMa. That robot transfers water between its front and rear to shift its weight distribution and help it negotiate obstacles.

sections.heading: A broad range of research
paragraphs: Other projects include an underwater quadruped, MIT’s automated optics laboratory and NASA’s Lunabotics competition, where students test robotic vehicles in simulated lunar-surface conditions.

sections.heading: How to read the collection
paragraphs: This is a set of videos from different projects, rather than a test of one product. Technical details and experimental results should be checked against the development teams and materials referenced by the original article.

anscer.title: ANSCER reports conditional FCC approval for three mobile robots
anscer.summary: The company says its AR250, AR650 and AR1250 models received conditional approval as it works toward US market access.

sections.heading: Three models named in the announcement
paragraphs: ANSCER Robotics says the AR250, AR650 and AR1250 received conditional FCC approval effective 18 September 2026. The report is a company announcement distributed through RoboticsTomorrow.

sections.heading: What it means for US operations
paragraphs: According to the announcement, the approval allows the company to pursue the equipment authorisations needed for US import and sales, subject to domestic manufacturing and supply-chain transparency conditions.

sections.heading: The approval remains conditional
paragraphs: The announcement distinguishes conditional approval from unconditional equipment authorisation and ties it to manufacturing commitments and continuing reporting. It should not be interpreted as an exemption from all requirements.

sections.heading: Applications for the robots
paragraphs: The AR family moves materials in warehouses, factories and intralogistics operations. The parent company is based in Bengaluru, India, while its Plano, Texas operation handles North American sales and service.

cassie.title: Tutor Intelligence introduces the next generation of Cassie and Sonny
cassie.summary: The company combines updated robot hardware and AI for case handling and individual-item picking in warehouses.

sections.heading: Tutor Intelligence’s robots
paragraphs: MassRobotics shared news of Tutor Intelligence’s next-generation Cassie and Sonny, covering hardware, AI models and deployments. This Cassie is Tutor’s robot, not Agility Robotics’ biped of the same name.

sections.heading: Cassie gains mobility on the factory floor
paragraphs: Cassie is a single-arm robot on a wheeled base for case picking, depalletising and stacking. The company says the new version can travel between stations autonomously, has an integrated vacuum system and adds two 3D LiDAR units for environmental sensing.

sections.heading: Sonny targets individual-item picking
paragraphs: Sonny uses a form focused on human-like dexterity and is intended to use the 4.5-billion-parameter Ti0 vision-language-action model. Initial tasks include warehouse navigation, shelf picking and delivering orders to packing stations.

sections.heading: Business model and claims
paragraphs: Tutor offers usage-based pricing and says the new robots have already been deployed at US facilities. Claims about deployment speed and returns come from the developer and do not guarantee the same results at every warehouse.

sections.heading: The small-drone operator role

sections.heading: An example of medical logistics
paragraphs: A separate video from an August exercise shows a heavy-lift drone delivering medical supplies to a simulated casualty-care location. It illustrates a logistics and medical-support application for drones.

amazon-greenwood-manufacturing-investmen.title: Amazon plans a $100 million-plus factory to support its robotics network
amazon-greenwood-manufacturing-investmen.summary: The Greenwood, Indiana facility will combine fabrication, robotic welding, coating and assembly, with a planned 2028 launch and 300 jobs.

sections.heading: A factory for the fulfillment network
paragraphs: Amazon announced on September 24 that it plans to invest more than $100 million in a roughly 585,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana. It will supply the North American fulfillment and robotics network, with a launch expected by 2028.

sections.heading: Several processes under one roof
paragraphs: Planned capabilities include fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly, supported by AWS, AI manufacturing systems and robotics. The announcement does not identify a particular robot model that the facility will manufacture.

sections.heading: Manufacturing and engineering jobs
paragraphs: Amazon expects 300 manufacturing and engineering positions, including CNC operators, welders, coating technicians, assemblers and controls engineers. The project combines automation investment with the people needed to operate and maintain production.

sections.heading: An announced investment, not an operating plant
paragraphs: The facility and opening date remain plans. The accompanying images and video illustrate Amazon’s existing robotics work. The Indiana project is separate from the Texas manufacturing investment announced earlier.

anymal-secure-door-access-whitegate-2026.title: ANYmal gains secure door access for industrial inspection
anymal-secure-door-access-whitegate-2026.summary: ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC tested automated access at Whitegate power station, combining robot credentials with existing site permissions.

sections.heading: Removing a route barrier
paragraphs: ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC are enabling ANYmal to pass through industrial doors, including access-controlled areas. The aim is to extend inspection routes without staff opening doors, while retaining the site’s safety barriers.

sections.heading: Two access mechanisms
paragraphs: At unlocked doors, radar triggers a dormakaba ED 100 or ED 250 operator. For locked doors, LEGIC digital credentials let the exos access system check authorization before unlocking. Operators can restrict permissions by zone, time window and task.

sections.heading: Tested in an operating power station
paragraphs: The companies report several weeks of testing at GE Vernova’s Whitegate power station in County Cork, Ireland. ANYmal requested access, crossed controlled doors and completed inspection routes without manual intervention in those steps, with timestamped records for auditing.

sections.heading: Existing security still matters
paragraphs: The system does not replace measures against people following an authorized user through a door. Existing site protections remain necessary. The access-control add-on is planned for later in 2026 for installed systems and future ANYmal hardware.

agility-confirms-wheeled-robot-explorati.title: Agility confirms early exploration of wheeled robots
agility-confirms-wheeled-robot-explorati.summary: Jonathan Hurst says the Digit developer is studying additional form factors. The wheeled design remains exploratory, with no product or launch date confirmed.

sections.heading: A new confirmation after the Digit 5 video
paragraphs: The Robot Report asked Jonathan Hurst about a wheeled robot rendering near the end of the Digit 5 launch video. His email confirmed that Agility is exploring several designs, including wheels. The new development is that confirmation, rather than another announcement of Digit 5.

sections.heading: Matching the form to the environment
paragraphs: Hurst said alternative approaches could bring robots to more environments sooner. The report contrasts wheels’ suitability for predictable, flat surfaces with the usefulness of legs around stairs, obstacles and uneven terrain.

sections.heading: No product definition yet
paragraphs: Asked whether this would be a wheeled Digit or a differently named and shaped robot, Hurst said it was too early to say and the work was just starting. Specifications, payload, reach, pricing and a market launch have not been confirmed.

sections.heading: A rendering is not a deployed prototype
paragraphs: The illustration comes from the existing launch video. It does not establish that a commercially ready wheeled prototype exists. Target tasks, physical testing and a decision to turn the exploration into a product remain developments to watch.

sections.heading: Coordinating mixed fleets
paragraphs: ASI’s Mobius platform is intended to coordinate equipment from different manufacturers, including haul trucks, dozers, loaders and compactors. Target applications include civil construction and material handling for infrastructure such as roads, airports and railways.

sections.heading: Deployment details remain open
paragraphs: The release describes the business expansion and platform capabilities, but does not identify a committed machine count, specific venture customers or a delivery timetable. Cost and productivity outcomes will need evidence from actual deployments.

leopard-lumotive-sirius-max-launch-2026.title: Sirius Max combines color and depth with programmable beam steering
leopard-lumotive-sirius-max-launch-2026.summary: Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced an RGB-D module for robotics, claiming depth sensing beyond 20 meters and one-megapixel depth resolution.

sections.heading: An integrated perception module
paragraphs: Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced Sirius Max, combining RGB imaging, indirect time-of-flight depth sensing and processing for robots and automation. The module is intended to supply synchronized color and depth information in real time.

sections.heading: Software controls where light goes
paragraphs: Lumotive’s TX10 transmitter and LCM technology steer illumination toward software-selected regions. The developers describe a fully solid-state design without moving mechanical parts, allowing sensing priorities to change instead of relying on fixed flood illumination.

sections.heading: One connection for imaging and control
paragraphs: The module uses an onsemi AF0130 depth sensor and GMSL2 to carry synchronized RGB video, depth and control over a coaxial cable. Proposed uses include navigation, mapping, cliff detection, collision avoidance and object handling.

sections.heading: Performance remains a manufacturer claim
paragraphs: Lumotive reports iToF operation beyond 20 meters indoors and outdoors with one-megapixel depth resolution. The announcement does not provide independent benchmarks, pricing or a delivery date. Performance still needs assessment with the actual materials, lighting and motion of a deployment.

ifr-world-robotics-2026-five-million.title: IFR reports five million industrial robots operating worldwide
ifr-world-robotics-2026-five-million.summary: World Robotics 2026 puts 2025 installations above 600,000, with China accounting for 59% and the United States becoming the second-largest market.

sections.heading: Installed stock and annual additions differ
paragraphs: IFR’s World Robotics 2026 report puts operational industrial-robot stock in 2025 at about five million, up 9%. New installations during that year exceeded 600,000, up 11%. These measure different things and should not be used interchangeably.

sections.heading: Asia’s markets moved in different directions
paragraphs: China installed about 354,000 robots, up 20%, representing 59% of global additions. Japan installed 36,219, down 19%; South Korea about 30,000, down 1%; and India nearly 10,500, up 15%. Growth was not uniform across the region.

sections.heading: The US moves into second place
paragraphs: US installations rose 12% to nearly 38,500, overtaking Japan to become the second-largest market after China. Germany remained Europe’s largest market, but additions fell 8% to fewer than 25,000. Italy, France and Spain also declined.

sections.heading: Forecasts are not completed installations
paragraphs: IFR forecasts 655,000 installations in 2026 and 806,000 in 2029, with labor shortages and supply-chain changes supporting demand. Those figures are projections rather than already recorded deployments.

skyebrowse-crush-claims-impact-crowd-202.summary: New workflows connect 3D scans to vehicle-damage measurements, editable collision scenes and estimated headcounts, while retaining human review.

sections.heading: From capture to reviewable measurements
paragraphs: SkyeBrowse released Crush Analysis, Claims and Crowd Counter to extend drone and phone capture beyond 3D model creation. Measurements and reports remain linked to the model so reviewers can inspect where damage measurements originated.

sections.heading: Vehicle damage and collision scenes
paragraphs: Crush Analysis aligns a scanned vehicle with a reference model and measures six crush stations. Impact combines multiple vehicles in an editable diagram with speed estimates and an animated collision replay. Evidence and assumptions still need review; the animation is not footage of the actual crash.

sections.heading: Claims supports screening
paragraphs: Claims assesses up to eight images to suggest parts for repair, replacement or further inspection, with cost and total-loss screening. The company says licensed adjusters and policy terms determine claim outcomes.

sections.heading: Crowd counting and access
paragraphs: Crowd Counter in the SkyeBrowse Flight App on DJI RC Pro estimates people visible in a drone photograph. Standard users receive three daily counts; Public Safety & Enterprise customers receive unlimited counts. Crush Analysis and Claims are free on all plans through October 31, 2026, then included with Public Safety & Enterprise models.

sections.heading: Recording more than camera images
paragraphs: The PolyUMI team released a preprint on September 24 describing a wireless handheld gripper that synchronizes wrist vision, optical touch, contact audio and motion state. It captures interaction details that an external camera may miss.

sections.heading: Sharing sensing between teaching and execution
paragraphs: The sensing finger transfers from the demonstration gripper to the robot in about ten minutes, preserving sensing geometry. Its reported parts cost is roughly $236; that is not the price of a complete robot or collection system.

sections.heading: Combining signals with VisTA

sections.heading: Limits of the evidence

sections.heading: When deployment hardware differs
paragraphs: Self-Adaptive VLA, released as a preprint on September 24, addresses hardware shifts such as joint-encoder offsets and actuation bias. These differences can make a trained policy fail at precision manipulation.

sections.heading: Using previous attempts as context
paragraphs: Training deliberately injects shifts and pairs rollout information with compensated expert demonstrations. A small encoder summarizes images, robot state and actions into context. Combining context from successive attempts helps condition the next attempt; correct expert demonstrations remain the training target.

sections.heading: A new-workstation demonstration
paragraphs: In a five-episode ring-assembly demonstration, the base policy succeeded five times at the original station and zero times after transfer. One failed trial as context produced two successes; two failed trials produced five. These are results for that demonstration, not guaranteed rates at other facilities.

sections.heading: A research method with deployment limits
paragraphs: Demonstrations cover ring assembly, corn transport, marker capping and tube insertion. Adaptation occurs across attempts, rather than repairing hardware or guaranteeing immediate recovery from every failure. Deployment still requires evaluating acceptable errors and task safety.

sections.heading: Testing is not a blanket safety guarantee

Simulation can expose weaknesses without putting people at risk, but cannot establish safety in every possible situation. yyforce-singapore-robotics-training-cent.summary: The center collects operational data and tests human–robot workflows while evaluating leasing and robotics-as-a-service models.

sections.heading: A service-workflow test center
paragraphs: YYForce announced the opening of its Robotics Training, Data and Experience Center in Singapore on October 6. It supports humanoid training, operational data collection, workflow testing and customer demonstrations for hospitality, cleaning, security, delivery and facility management, drawing on the company’s existing workforce services.

sections.heading: Learning from simulated workplaces
paragraphs: Test environments cover housekeeping, restroom cleaning, banqueting and hospitality support. Data includes navigation, motion, object interaction and environmental conditions. The center evaluates collaboration between people, humanoids and specialized robots. A security command center also demonstrates patrol robots integrated with cameras, sensors and central monitoring.

sections.heading: Commercial capability remains under evaluation
paragraphs: YYForce explicitly says training does not establish autonomous completion of full housekeeping or restroom-cleaning duties. It is assessing RaaS, leasing and managed-service arrangements but has not announced material robotics orders or recurring revenue from these proposed models. Viability depends on productivity, service quality, maintenance costs and required human intervention.

exotec-first-supply-next-morning-results.title: First Supply reports Skypod results supporting next-morning delivery
exotec-first-supply-next-morning-results.summary: The company-reported results describe 10-times-faster picking and more than 14,000 SKUs after over a year of operation.

sections.heading: Results after more than a year
paragraphs: Exotec published First Supply’s Skypod operating results on October 6, after more than a year of use. The reported service milestone is next-morning delivery for orders placed by 5 p.m. First Supply distributes HVAC, plumbing, lighting and industrial products whose availability affects contractors’ schedules.

sections.heading: Picking performance and storage headroom
paragraphs: The release reports more than 14,000 SKUs in the system and picking speeds ten times those of previous manual processes. Vertical storage reduces operator travel. Fourfold storage-capacity growth within the existing racking footprint is expansion potential, not an already completed fourfold increase. These figures are supplier-and-customer claims rather than an independent benchmark.

sections.heading: Service outcomes matter alongside speed
paragraphs: First Supply says next-day demand can represent up to 20% of daily distribution-center volume, making overnight replenishment operationally important. However, the announcement does not detail the tenfold comparison methodology or total costs needed for a payback calculation. Other operators should compare the case with their own product mix and peak-demand patterns.

robco-billion-valuation-alfie-launch-pla.title: RobCo reaches billion-dollar valuation ahead of planned Alfie launch
robco-billion-valuation-alfie-launch-pla.summary: The transaction combines new investment with an employee secondary sale as RobCo expands US operations and prepares its industrial robot.

sections.heading: Valuation is different from capital raised
paragraphs: RobCo’s valuation exceeded $1 billion in a transaction first reported on October 5 and covered by Modern Materials Handling on October 6. It combines investment in the company with a secondary share sale for employees. The valuation is not a billion-dollar fundraising amount. Participants include existing investors such as Sequoia and Lightspeed and new investors including Cherry Ventures.

sections.heading: Alfie is scheduled for 2027
paragraphs: RobCo plans Alfie’s commercial launch at its RobCoN summit in Munich on March 4, 2027. The company describes an industrial robot combining perception, reasoning and execution for variable factory tasks. That is a product positioning and development goal, not independent proof that it can handle every industrial workflow without preparation.

sections.heading: US operations are expanding
paragraphs: The company reports customer operations across more than a dozen states, manufacturing and assembly in Austin, and a San Francisco lab. CEO Roman Hölzl has relocated to the US. Local operations may support deployment and service, but practical value still depends on application reliability, safety and total costs. The announced commercial launch remains a future milestone.

boston-dynamics-rohit-prasad-ceo-2026.title: Boston Dynamics appoints Rohit Prasad CEO effective October 7
boston-dynamics-rohit-prasad-ceo-2026.summary: The former Amazon AI leader will guide the company’s integration of AI and robotics and its commercialization efforts.

sections.heading: A leadership change takes effect
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics announced on October 6 that Rohit Prasad will become chief executive officer effective October 7, 2026. The stated focus is integrating advanced AI with robotics and expanding commercial applications. This is a distinct corporate development from the previously covered Atlas hand announcement.

sections.heading: Experience in AI product development
paragraphs: Prasad previously served as an Amazon senior vice president and head scientist for Alexa and Artificial General Intelligence. During twelve years there he helped develop Alexa and later the Amazon Nova foundation-model family. Earlier, he spent nearly fourteen years at Raytheon BBN Technologies working on machine learning and its applications.

sections.heading: Strategy does not establish new capabilities
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics identifies Spot for inspection, Stretch for box handling and electric Atlas as a platform in development. The leadership announcement gives no new product delivery schedule or demonstrated technical capability. Prasad’s expected board appointment remains subject to approval. Commercial and technical progress must therefore be assessed separately from the strategic intent of the hire.

sereact-zalando-ceva-live-returns-2026.title: Sereact robots enter live Zalando returns operations in Germany and Poland
sereact-zalando-ceva-live-returns-2026.summary: Cortex-powered dual-arm systems are operating with CEVA in Greven and Świebodzin under a RaaS model, handling unpredictable fashion returns.

sections.heading: Two operational sites
paragraphs: On October 7, Sereact, Zalando and CEVA Logistics announced that dual-arm robots had entered live operations at Greven in Germany and Świebodzin in Poland. These sites are the first operational step in a broader European returns initiative. The development is a production deployment, following Zalando’s participation as a strategic investor in Sereact’s Series B in July.

sections.heading: Handling unfamiliar returns
paragraphs: Fashion returns often arrive crumpled or poorly packed, making fixed picking sequences difficult to apply. According to the partners, Cortex identifies, grasps and sorts unfamiliar objects without training separately for each article or relying on a predefined SKU set. The focus is adapting manipulation to the condition of each incoming item, rather than assuming identical presentation.

sections.heading: Service model and evidence limits
paragraphs: The deployment uses Robotics-as-a-Service, with the aim of reducing repetitive handling and physical strain. Employees remain responsible for station supervision, exceptions and quality control. The announcement does not provide robot counts, hourly throughput or independently measured error rates, so it does not establish a quantified cost saving or readiness for every warehouse environment.

ncsu-feather-star-two-actuator-swimmer-2.title: Feather-star robot moves through 3D space underwater with two actuators
ncsu-feather-star-two-actuator-swimmer-2.summary: NC State researchers use flexible wings for swimming, hovering and turning, demonstrating camera exploration and lifting while a wireless version remains future work.

sections.heading: Structure does part of the work
paragraphs: NC State reported research published in Science Advances on October 7. Four flexible wings surround a central disk containing two actuators. Each wing returns to its original shape after bending. This mechanical design produces several motion patterns from a small number of inputs, reducing the need for a separate actuator for every direction.

sections.heading: Three modes enable maneuvering
paragraphs: Driving both actuators makes the wings pulse to raise the robot; slower flapping enables hovering and stopping lets it descend. Driving one actuator creates fish-like propulsion, while rapidly alternating the two produces rotation. The paper’s abstract reports a maximum swimming speed of 1.64 body lengths per second and a peak rotation rate of 90 degrees per second.

sections.heading: Demonstrations and remaining work
paragraphs: The researchers demonstrated underwater camera exploration and object lifting, both individually and with multiple robots. These experiments show platform capabilities rather than commercial performance at sea. A fully wireless version is a future direction, and the team is seeking collaboration with specialists in other fields to develop suitable applications.

mecka-series-b-60m-data-deployment-2026.summary: Sequoia leads the Series B with NVIDIA, M12, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung among the new investors, supporting human-demonstration capture and robot integration.

sections.heading: Funding the data and deployment stack
paragraphs: Mecka announced a $60 million Series B on October 7, led by Sequoia Capital. New investors include NVIDIA, Microsoft’s M12, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung, alongside continued support from Kindred, Framework Ventures and Neo. The funding will expand data infrastructure, the internal research lab and commercial robot deployment.

sections.heading: Recording physical experience
paragraphs: Mecka designs its own multisensor capture hardware and runs recording operations in homes and commercial settings. Its models turn those recordings into motion information, 3D reconstruction and aligned signals. The company focuses on physical experience, including grasping and contact, that robotics teams need to train machines for real tasks.

sections.heading: Integration and financial qualifications
paragraphs: Its integration approach combines hardware, on-site data capture, post-training and ongoing operation. Mecka says it exceeded a $100 million annualized revenue run rate in June and projects $300 million by year-end. These are company-reported figures and forecasts; a run rate is not a full year of recognized revenue. The announcement also does not independently verify robot improvement across every task.

sections.heading: AMRs lead the rollout
paragraphs: A joint announcement dated October 7 describes a distribution agreement giving TD SYNNEX partners access to KUKA Group’s autonomous mobile robots. The rollout starts in the UK, France, Spain and Benelux, with more markets planned in subsequent quarters. Collaborative robots, education packages and industrial software are expected to follow as the relationship develops.

sections.heading: Connecting IT partners with operations
paragraphs: The agreement targets partners already serving manufacturing, logistics, e-commerce, healthcare and automotive customers. The companies want to connect operational equipment with AI, cloud, edge computing and data infrastructure. Its main significance is broadening the channel that can deliver automation projects; it is not an announcement of a new robot model.

sections.heading: Support and current scope
paragraphs: Partner engagement begins immediately in the launch markets, including business briefings, technical workshops and training online and through KUKA Colleges. Local-language sessions and learning paths will be supported through PartnerFirst. No pricing, installation count or Thailand rollout date is given, so local distribution coverage and support still need to be established.

danaher-abcam-autonomous-lab-plan-2026.title: Danaher plans an AI and robotics lab for iterative reagent development
danaher-abcam-autonomous-lab-plan-2026.summary: The Abcam-based lab targets scaled operation in early 2027, with Automata supporting orchestration and robotics; the claimed eightfold speedup is a design goal.

sections.heading: Starting with research reagents
paragraphs: Danaher announced its first planned AI-powered autonomous lab on October 7. Based at Abcam, it is expected to operate at scale in early 2027. The initial focus is affinity reagents, including antibodies and other molecular research tools that bind specific biological targets. This is a research-infrastructure announcement, not the launch of a patient-ready medicine.

sections.heading: A connected experimental loop
paragraphs: AI helps propose molecules, after which the lab builds and tests them and feeds results into the next design cycle. The workflow combines technologies from Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies and Molecular Devices. Automata collaborates on instrument orchestration and robotic automation, while scientists continue to make the key decisions.

sections.heading: Targets remain to be demonstrated
paragraphs: The lab is designed to move from an idea to a validated reagent up to eight times faster and increase annual reagent generation by up to tenfold, from tens to hundreds as it scales. These are forward-looking targets rather than a completed year of operating results. Each design is intended to be tested and verified so that speed does not replace scientific rigor.

overview-ov-spark-agentic-inspection-lau.title: Overview AI launches OV Spark inspection cameras with an onboard assistant
overview-ov-spark-agentic-inspection-lau.summary: Ten inspection tools and the Sparky assistant help configure checks, with on-device production inspection and an early deployment at MEC.

sections.heading: Setup built around the part
paragraphs: Overview AI launched OV Spark and Spark Pro on October 6 with Sparky, an assistant for choosing inspection tools and explaining results in English. Ten tools cover tasks such as counting, OCR, segmentation, anomaly detection, measurement and barcodes. Alignment makes inspection regions follow a shifting or rotating part, and an absent part causes capture failure rather than an empty-frame pass.

sections.heading: On-camera operation
paragraphs: Spark provides 1.2-megapixel imaging and Pro provides 5 megapixels, using Qualcomm Dragonwing processing in a 70 × 116 × 53 mm IP66-rated body. Model training, inference, the operator interface and PLC communication run on the device. The product documentation says production inspection and Sparky do not require cloud connectivity, while optional Defect Studio synthetic-image generation uses the cloud.

sections.heading: Early factory use and validation
paragraphs: Mansfield Engineered Components uses the camera at an end-of-line station previously checked visually, where a missing washer is a frequent defect. The products are available directly and through partners. Users still need to train applicable tools and validate lighting, cycle time and result integration. Product documentation also excludes instance segmentation for separating overlapping objects and judging them individually.

paragraphs: Areas under evaluation include precision assembly, robotic loading and unloading of test equipment, and autonomous material movement. Universal Robots cobots, board testers and Bright Machines’ platform would contribute different data streams to a unit’s production history. The aim is to connect design choices with assembly execution and measured electrical performance.

sections.heading: A phased integration effort
paragraphs: Bright Machines told The Robot Report that it had begun adding Universal Robots to its lines and identifying technical integration areas. Work will proceed in phases tied to customer applications and requirements; no complete-system timeline has been announced. Its record of more than 130 microfactory deployments in over 10 countries predates this deal and is not a deployment count for the new collaboration.

twelvelabs-pegasus16-egocentric-video-la.summary: TwelveLabs adds action segmentation, descriptions and clip assessment to support behavioral datasets, without replacing tactile sensors or robot control.

sections.heading: Understanding the operator’s viewpoint
paragraphs: TwelveLabs released Pegasus 1.6 on October 6 with support for video captured from the viewpoint of the person or machine doing a task, such as assembly, cooking or robot teleoperation. It also improves entity recognition and handles still images through the same API as video. The company does not require a proprietary capture camera.

sections.heading: Preparing reviewable datasets
paragraphs: Supported workflows include timed action labels, detailed captions, quality scoring, search for rare events or duplicate clips, and flagging faces, bystanders or sensitive data. These tools help teams organize raw footage for review and training selection. Flagging is an aid to review; it does not itself establish consent or guarantee compliance in every situation.

sections.heading: Video analysis has a defined role
paragraphs: Pegasus identifies visible behavior, such as what each hand is doing and how a scene changes, for teams to combine with their own sensor data. It does not replace tactile or actuator-level sensing or make a robot execute a task simply by reading footage. The reviewed announcement provides no independent, across-task measurement of improved robot success rates.

paragraphs: Wing and Walmart announced on October 5 that Denver and Seattle will join their delivery network in 2027, bringing the expansion plan close to 20 major US metro areas. munson-blueflite-phase-two-medical-drone.summary: Phase two in Michigan runs October 6–30, simulating transport of supplies, lab samples and medicines to gather evidence for rural healthcare logistics.

paragraphs: An October 5 announcement describes the second project phase led by Traverse Connect, Munson Healthcare, blueflite and Central Michigan University’s Rural Health Excellence Institute. paragraphs: The May 9–20, 2025 phase completed nearly 70 flights within a one-mile radius of Munson Medical Center. The new phase extends flight duration and introduces multiple aircraft and sensor technology. The partners report FAA approval, but the announcement does not list every operational condition and should not be read as permission for unrestricted flights anywhere.

sections.heading: Evidence before broader deployment
paragraphs: The pilot collects operating data to assess how air transport can connect rural healthcare facilities. Support comes from Michigan’s Advanced Aerial Mobility Activation Fund and Newlab. Phase-two results are intended to inform scaling decisions; there are not yet reported outcome figures from this phase showing reductions in treatment time, cost or errors.

aws-physical-ai-toolchain-launch-2026.summary: The open-source workflow combines AWS and NVIDIA components for data generation, model training, simulation, edge deployment and continued improvement.

sections.heading: Connecting the development stages
paragraphs: AWS introduced its Physical AI Toolchain on October 8, bringing together synthetic data generation, training, simulation and validation, edge deployment, and continued improvement. Developers can adopt individual components or an integrated workflow. The announcement packages existing technologies into a more cohesive development process; it does not introduce a new robot model.

sections.heading: Cloud training and physical deployment
paragraphs: Amazon SageMaker supports model training, while AWS IoT Greengrass distributes models to edge devices. The NVIDIA stack includes Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac GR00T and Cosmos. Data collected during robot operations can feed subsequent cloud training cycles. AWS describes the approach as hardware-neutral, rather than prescribing a particular robot form factor or manufacturer.

sections.heading: Production readiness remains application-specific
paragraphs: Simulation and synthetic data support testing, but do not guarantee real-world performance in every situation. AWS guidance requires users to test, secure and optimize sample components before production use, and cloud resources may incur charges. The launch does not provide a universal benchmark establishing success rates across all robot hardware.

sections.heading: Different applications are at different stages
paragraphs: The platform spans L2–L4 automotive programs and heavy-equipment perception projects progressing toward production. Helm.ai also describes delivery-drone work and broader robotics ambitions, without publishing deployment counts by application. doe-four-lab-robotics-testbeds-selection.title: DOE selects four laboratory robotics projects to build reusable autonomy
doe-four-lab-robotics-testbeds-selection.summary: Argonne, Brookhaven, Oak Ridge and SLAC lead complementary testbeds, with funding subject to negotiations and future appropriations.

sections.heading: Shared infrastructure for scientific facilities
paragraphs: The US Department of Energy’s Office of Science selected four projects to advance robotics and automation for scientific infrastructure. Intended outputs include open software, interfaces, reusable robot skills, datasets and models, alongside safety methods and experiment provenance. The objective is infrastructure other laboratories can extend, rather than four isolated demonstrations.

sections.heading: Complementary roles across four laboratories
paragraphs: Argonne’s MAESTRO will develop infrastructure that improves through experience. Brookhaven’s DART will examine failures, reliability and skill transfer across robotic platforms. Oak Ridge’s TRACE will connect robots, instruments and data through standardized interfaces. SLAC’s SPIRE will combine sample manipulation, detectors and controls in photon- and electron-science facilities.

sections.heading: Funding and validation are conditional
paragraphs: The announcement identifies $30 million in total funding, including $2 million in fiscal 2026, with later funding dependent on congressional appropriations. Selection starts award negotiations and does not guarantee an award. Success must still be demonstrated through transfer across instruments and laboratories, as well as valid scientific outcomes from automated experiments.

tecnalia-zutik-industrial-humanoid-resea.title: ZUTIK researches software for humanoids integrated with factory systems
tecnalia-zutik-industrial-humanoid-resea.summary: TECNALIA leads six research organizations developing navigation, manipulation and OT/IT integration, targeting TRL 4 laboratory demonstrators.

sections.heading: Adapting existing platforms
paragraphs: TECNALIA described ZUTIK as a research effort to prepare Basque industry for reliable humanoid integration. The project will develop algorithms and software components for existing robot platforms rather than build a new humanoid. It addresses complex factory environments, object handling and coordinated whole-body motion.

sections.heading: A modular integration architecture
paragraphs: Research covers perception, bipedal locomotion, safe navigation, multi-fingered and whole-body manipulation, and skill-based programming. A modular, vendor-agnostic architecture is intended to connect these capabilities with factory OT/IT systems. The aim is to coordinate humanoids within existing production infrastructure and support future integration across platforms.

sections.heading: Laboratory validation comes first
paragraphs: The consortium includes TECNALIA, AUTOTECH ENGINEERING, IKERLAN, MONDRAGON MU-EPS, EHU and INVEMA, with eight industrial companies contributing through a business committee. TRL 4 laboratory demonstrators will use scenarios such as kitting, assembly, inspection in complex spaces and internal logistics. Further readiness work will be required before production deployment.

Company representatives described a payload limit of about five pounds, or 2.3 kilograms. Aircraft fly at roughly 300 feet, or 91 meters, and lower pods on a tether to backyards or other designated delivery locations.

sections.heading: Expansion remains a plan
paragraphs: The company expects to expand across the city and wider Austin area, without a published date for every neighborhood. Its relationship with the school, which offers drone aviation courses, is at an early stage and may support engineering or robotics education. elmo-secure-development-ml2-certificatio.title: Elmo receives IEC 62443-4-1 ML2 secure-development certification
elmo-secure-development-ml2-certificatio.summary: TÜV SÜD certified the motion-control supplier’s development lifecycle, covering documented security processes and post-release vulnerability handling.

sections.heading: Certification of the supplier’s process
paragraphs: Elmo Motion Control announced on October 7 that TÜV SÜD certified its secure product-development lifecycle to IEC 62443-4-1 Maturity Level 2. Elmo supplies servo drives, multi-axis controllers and motors for applications including robotics and AGVs. The certification provides evidence for supplier assessments involving components integrated into automated equipment.

sections.heading: From design to maintenance
paragraphs: The program includes threat modeling during design, mandatory peer code review and independent security testing before release. Formal vulnerability and patch processes continue after release, with communication to customers. ML2 recognizes documented, repeatable development practices carried out by trained and qualified personnel.

sections.heading: What the certification does not establish
paragraphs: This part of the standard evaluates development practices, not whether an entire robot installation is vulnerability-free. Machine builders must still assess networking, connected equipment and update procedures in their own systems. Elmo says the program supports preparation for European cybersecurity requirements; it does not certify every compliance obligation of a customer’s finished machine.

scouts-vidullanka-first-solar-deployment.title: Scouts discloses autonomous drone monitoring at Vidullanka solar plants
scouts-vidullanka-first-solar-deployment.summary: New reports describe a September deployment combining 4K and thermal cameras with automated docking at two Sri Lankan solar facilities.

sections.heading: A first-customer deployment is disclosed
paragraphs: Reports published on October 8–9 describe Scouts’ aerial-monitoring installation for Vidullanka PLC in Sri Lanka. Deployment was completed in September, rather than on the reporting date. According to the partners, Vidullanka is the first customer of this autonomous system, which operates at two solar plants with a combined capacity of four megawatts.

sections.heading: An integrated monitoring service
paragraphs: The installation combines an automated drone, a weatherproof docking and charging station, and anomaly-detection software. Its 4K and thermal cameras support checks for damaged fencing, vegetation encroachment, maintenance needs and fire risks. Scouts describes locally managed hardware, software and services intended to provide situational information to personnel on the ground.

sections.heading: Operational evidence remains limited
paragraphs: The partners say aerial coverage can reduce continuous ground-patrol work and help staff respond. The reports do not provide flight counts, false-alarm rates or independently verified cost comparisons. This is an infrastructure deployment example, but it does not establish all-weather performance or demonstrate that security personnel can be replaced entirely.

sections.heading: A computing and control unit
paragraphs: RobotX AI introduced Xmind on October 8 as a computing and control unit connecting robot sensors, control systems and AI models. The Irvine-based company targets industrial inspection, firefighting, education, security and data collection. This is a company product announcement, rather than an independent validation of operating performance.

sections.heading: Linking perception, instructions and actions
paragraphs: Advertised capabilities include visual perception, environmental understanding, voice instruction handling, AI task planning, multimodal processing and hardware adaptation. A shared robot-intelligence architecture still requires integration and application customization for physical machines. The announcement does not establish plug-and-play support for every robot or task.

sections.heading: Demonstrations and unresolved specifications
paragraphs: RobotX AI plans hardware demonstrations at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on October 13–15 and reports $3 million in seed funding for development and expansion. kawasaki-cp110l-north-america-launch-pla.summary: The regional debut is scheduled for PACK EXPO, with its 2,200-case-per-hour rating tied to specified payload and motion conditions.

sections.heading: A regional rollout milestone
paragraphs: Kawasaki Robotics USA announced on October 8 that the CP110L would make its North American debut at PACK EXPO in Chicago on October 18–21. This is a regional rollout following the global launch on February 16. The target applications are packaging and end-of-line operations constrained by floor space and ceiling height.

sections.heading: Payload and speed are different ratings
paragraphs: The four-axis robot has a maximum payload of 110 kilograms, a 2,505-mm reach and ±0.05-mm repeatability. The 2,200-case-per-hour rating applies at 60 kilograms including the gripper, using a motion pattern with a 400-mm rise, 2,000-mm horizontal travel and 400-mm descent. It is not a guaranteed rate at maximum payload or in every cell layout.

sections.heading: Compact architecture still needs integration
paragraphs: Kawasaki specifies a required ceiling height of 2,242 mm and a revolute-axis interference radius of 453 mm. A hollow wrist routes cables and hoses internally, while regeneration reuses energy from deceleration. The robot weighs 820 kilograms, so integrators still need to validate mounting, tooling, safety clearances and actual cycle times. Regional pricing was not announced.

sections.heading: Automating inspection-region setup
paragraphs: TECNALIA and AUTIS reported progress on AI-generated inspection masks for detecting paint defects on vehicle bodies. Specialists traditionally define these image regions manually for each vehicle model and installation. The work targets setup effort when commissioning visual-inspection systems; it does not introduce a painting robot or a new camera product.

sections.heading: A varied development dataset
paragraphs: Segmentation models generate masks from images captured by inspection systems. Development involved more than 650 images from six manufacturers, 20 vehicle models, eight plants and 13 production lines. This diversity supported evaluation across different industrial settings. The number of plants represented in the data is not a count of newly installed commercial products.

sections.heading: Feasibility without a quantified benchmark
paragraphs: TECNALIA says the results demonstrate technical feasibility and reduce configuration effort. The team also identified consistent labeling criteria as important for improving generalization. The announcement does not provide accuracy percentages, measured time savings or a separate test-set breakdown. Factories therefore need application-specific evaluation before drawing conclusions about their own returns.

sections.heading: Counting completed picks

sections.heading: Hardware and software
paragraphs: Danu separates hardware purchase from software licensing and claims gripper replacement in 20 minutes. These are existing company product descriptions, not independent tests or newly launched specifications.

abb-irb1700-irb1700id-launch-2026.title: ABB launches IRB 1700 and 1700ID for precision manufacturing
abb-irb1700-irb1700id-launch-2026.summary: Five variants carry 6–12 kilograms; performance improvements remain manufacturer claims.

sections.heading: New manufacturing models
paragraphs: ABB announced the IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID for their public debut at CIIF in Shanghai on October 12–16. Five variants carry 6–12 kilograms and use OmniCore controllers, targeting handling, welding, finishing and machine tending.

sections.heading: Accuracy and installation
paragraphs: ABB specifies path repeatability down to 0.03 millimetres and joint speeds up to 700 degrees per second. The footprint is 50% smaller than the predecessor, while the 1700ID routes cables and hoses internally.

sections.heading: Validate on the intended task
paragraphs: Claims include up to 20% shorter cycles, 15% lower power consumption and oil-change intervals up to 20,000 hours. These manufacturer figures do not guarantee every cell’s results; tooling, paths and production timing still matter.

abb-eyemotion-ai-robot-trainer-integrati.title: ABB integrates AI Robot Trainer with OmniCore EyeMotion
abb-eyemotion-ai-robot-trainer-integrati.summary: An integrated workflow connects image collection, training, deployment and robot motion.

sections.heading: One training and deployment loop
paragraphs: ABB is extending OmniCore EyeMotion with AI Robot Trainer to connect image collection, model training, deployment and improvement. Integrators can adapt vision applications across production lines with less dependence on AI specialists.

sections.heading: Turning perception into movement
paragraphs: The workflow combines real and synthetic images, guided steps and a chatbot. It addresses changes in products, lighting and layouts, and connects to automatic collision-free path planning for picking, inspection, sorting and assembly.

sections.heading: Conditional performance claims
paragraphs: ABB claims up to 90% less commissioning time and 50% shorter cycles when combined with collision-free path planning. The announcement provides no independent evaluation; results should be checked using the intended parts and production images.

asimov-menlo-python-sdk-release-2026.title: Asimov releases the open-source Menlo Python SDK
asimov-menlo-python-sdk-release-2026.summary: The SDK is public; the announced Edge source release remains separately unconfirmed.

sections.heading: Connecting applications to a robot
paragraphs: Menlo Research released Menlo SDK for Asimov 1. Python applications can issue walking and joint commands, read robot state, and access cameras and audio. The public repository uses Apache 2.0 and requires Python 3.12 or later.

sections.heading: Local and remote connections
paragraphs: LiveKit supports internet connections, while UDP serves local applications. The announcement demonstrates upper-body motions, VR teleoperation and a locomotion-policy loop that reads robot state and returns joint commands.

sections.heading: Control priority is not an emergency stop
paragraphs: The team also announced open-sourcing Asimov Edge, which arbitrates control sources; that source release remains unconfirmed in the reviewed evidence. Documentation gives Cockpit and gamepad priority over SDK applications and explicitly says the SDK is not an emergency stop.

paragraphs: Aaron Saunders announced on LinkedIn that Google DeepMind is building a Cambridge-area robotics lab for the hardware team developed since he joined a year earlier. Recruitment context identifies Cambridge, Massachusetts; the facility has not been announced as operational.

sections.heading: Recruiting builders and researchers
paragraphs: The post invites machinists, engineers and researchers to join. It highlights the physical facilities and hardware skills needed alongside AI research. Saunders previously served as Boston Dynamics’ chief technology officer before joining DeepMind in 2025.

sections.heading: Details still undisclosed
paragraphs: The announcement gives no building size, budget, exact address or new robot model. More news in 2027 does not establish an opening or product-launch date. The publisher’s AI-generated illustration does not show the lab’s actual location.

sections.heading: From task intent to movement
paragraphs: Archon’s roughly three-minute Whole-Body Intelligence debut describes S1 for task understanding and multimodal input, and S0 for coordinated execution and stabilization. The aim is to connect manipulation with whole-body posture and movement.

sections.heading: Learning from demonstrations and corrections
paragraphs: The company describes human-data pretraining followed by real-robot training and DAgger corrective examples. Footage shows AGIBOT A3, Booster T2 and modified Unitree G1 robots; their presence together does not prove shared weights or cooperative task execution.

sections.heading: Reading the footage carefully

sections.heading: People still feed the station
paragraphs: Two robot arms fold at a table rather than on a walking humanoid. A person supplies each new shirt, so the demonstration measures a human-fed folding station, not an unattended washing, drying and storage workflow.

sections.heading: No common fastest-in-industry test

benewake-nova20-near-field-lidar-launch-.title: Benewake launches NOVA20 for near-field robot sensing
benewake-nova20-near-field-lidar-launch-.summary: A 20-point sensor covers 0.05–1 metre as a complement to cameras and longer-range LiDAR.

sections.heading: Closing a near-field gap
paragraphs: Benewake introduced NOVA20 for the metre surrounding a robot, complementing longer-range LiDAR and cameras that the robot’s body can obscure. It outputs physical distance measurements rather than two-dimensional images.

sections.heading: Compact solid-state sensing
paragraphs: Specifications list 20 detection points, a 40-degree field of view, 0.05–1 metre range, weight below 5 grams and power below 1 watt. The one-metre specification assumes 10% target reflectivity under 100-klux lighting.

sections.heading: Applications and system limits
paragraphs: Proposed uses include wall-following, detecting stairs or drop-offs, and slowing before contact with people. Sensors can sit on chassis or limbs. These component claims do not establish that a complete robot automatically meets safety requirements.

amap-sands-tutu-robot-guides-delivery-20.summary: The Macau resort deployment builds on NBA House service and planned indoor navigation.

sections.heading: From an event to resort services
paragraphs: Amap and Sands China marked the first Tutu delivery at NBA House in The Venetian, Macau, on October 10. The quadrupeds will guide resort visitors, alongside planned indoor navigation and 3D previews of selected areas in Amap.

sections.heading: Reported service activity
paragraphs: The release reports 214 direction requests and 4,546 Chinese- and English-language questions during an 11-hour workday. Tutu robots reportedly travelled over 40 kilometres collectively; these are organizer figures, not independently verified per-robot results.

sections.heading: Sustained service remains the next test
paragraphs: Resort operation adds longer service periods, more destinations and staff coordination. stryker-cmr-versius-equity-alliance-2026.title: Stryker plans a roughly $400 million CMR Surgical investment
stryker-cmr-versius-equity-alliance-2026.summary: The alliance includes U.S. sales rights and a future acquisition option, subject to conditions.

sections.heading: Investment with a future option
paragraphs: Stryker and CMR Surgical announced a planned preferred-equity investment of approximately $400 million, or £300 million. Stryker also receives an exclusive future option to acquire the remaining equity under agreed terms; a full acquisition has not closed.

sections.heading: Sharing commercial responsibilities
paragraphs: Stryker will be the exclusive U.S. sales agent for the Versius portfolio. CMR retains product development and commercialization outside the United States, combining its soft-tissue robotics expertise with Stryker’s commercial network.

sections.heading: Conditions and clinical limits
paragraphs: The companies highlight Versius’s modular operating-room design, but this announcement is not comparative clinical evidence. Regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions remain, and commercial expansion should not be confused with demonstrated treatment superiority or authorization in every country.

jaka-kargo50-zu50-ciif-debut-2026.title: JAKA introduces Kargo50 and Zu50 for heavier factory work
jaka-kargo50-zu50-ciif-debut-2026.summary: The wheeled platform targets tote handling; the separate Zu50 arm carries 50 kilograms.

sections.heading: Two approaches to factory handling
paragraphs: JAKA announced the wheeled Kargo50 humanoid and Zu50 collaborative arm for an October 12 CIIF debut in Shanghai. Kargo50 targets tote and material transfer, while Zu50 extends the company’s higher-payload arm range.

sections.heading: Keep model specifications separate
paragraphs: Pandaily cites a 50-kilogram payload and 2,100-millimetre reach for Zu50, but no verified Kargo50 payload specification. A claimed improvement from 105 to 28 seconds per tote belongs to the earlier Kargo10 and must not be attributed to the new model.

sections.heading: Demonstrations versus deployment results
paragraphs: A factory-style booth pairs wheeled robots for engine transport and screw tightening, with JAKA EVO linking task planning to motion control. Demonstrations and manufacturer claims still require validation for each customer’s speed, durability and cost requirements.

promise-drhorton-1250-homes-agreement-20.title: Promise Robotics signs D.R. Horton agreement for more than 1,250 homes
promise-drhorton-1250-homes-agreement-20.summary: A multi-year agreement gives the homebuilder access to robotic production capacity without building its own factories.

sections.heading: A multi-year production agreement
paragraphs: Promise Robotics announced a commercial agreement with D.R. Horton to support production of more than 1,250 homes through Factory-as-a-Service. Promise calls it the first major US homebuilder on the platform as its US factory network expands.

sections.heading: Connecting designs with production
paragraphs: The platform converts existing home designs into production plans and robot instructions, then coordinates manufacturing, factory operations and site installation. Builders gain access to capacity without developing and operating their own automated factories.

sections.heading: Delivery results remain to be measured
paragraphs: The aim is greater capacity and more predictable cycles amid labour constraints. The agreed home count is not a completed-build count; the release provides neither project-level delivery schedules nor independently verified cost savings.

scan-olo-browser-robotics-partnership-20.title: Scan and OLO partner on browser-based Unitree robot deployment
scan-olo-browser-robotics-partnership-20.summary: The partnership combines hardware and AI infrastructure with browser tools for teleoperation, simulation and navigation.

sections.heading: Hardware meets deployment software
paragraphs: Scan Computers and Sheffield-based OLO Robotics are combining Scan’s robots, AI infrastructure and technical services with OLO’s browser platform. Target applications include industrial inspection, research and prototyping.

sections.heading: Test before deployment
paragraphs: Built on ROS 2, OLO brings together teleoperation, simulation, sensor monitoring and autonomous navigation. Teams can develop and test behaviour virtually before deploying it on Unitree robots supplied by Scan, using browser-based tools.

sections.heading: A lower starting barrier
paragraphs: The partners aim to reduce the initial dependence on specialist ROS developers, not prove that every installation needs no engineering. No measured deployment times or safety results are reported. A demonstration is planned at Scan booth 3068 at GTC Berlin, October 20–22.

yyforce-novotel-mercure-service-robot-ro.title: YYForce plans service robots at two Singapore on Stevens hotels
yyforce-novotel-mercure-service-robot-ro.summary: Deliveries, cleaning and concierge support come first; humanoid housekeeping remains a later research programme.

sections.heading: A two-hotel operating environment
paragraphs: YYForce, Novotel Singapore on Stevens and Mercure Singapore on Stevens announced a partnership across 772 guestrooms, restaurants and event spaces. The service-robot rollout is confirmed, but the release explicitly says deployment has not begun.

sections.heading: Prepare the building interfaces
paragraphs: Phase one covers specialist robots for guest deliveries, food-and-beverage transport, scheduled cleaning and concierge directions. Lift integration, routes, networking and arrival notifications must be prepared, with tasks matched to capability and technical readiness.

sections.heading: Savings are projections
paragraphs: A pre-deployment model projects roughly 10% lower monthly costs in selected operations, including robot costs; this is not a measured outcome. Later research would use permitted observations of housekeeping and banquet work, not establish autonomous cleaning of occupied guestrooms.

dominion-tencore-canadian-termit-product.title: Dominion and TENCORE plan Canadian TerMIT production for 2027
dominion-tencore-canadian-termit-product.summary: An MoU covers manufacturing transfer and AuraNet integration; definitive agreements remain to be completed.

sections.heading: An initial memorandum
paragraphs: Ottawa-based Dominion Dynamics and Ukraine’s TENCORE signed an MoU to manufacture TerMIT uncrewed ground vehicles in Canada and integrate Dominion’s AuraNet. The AUSA 2026 signing in Washington targets initial production in 2027.

sections.heading: Manufacturing transfer and training
paragraphs: A TENCORE team will lead technology transfer and train Canadian technicians. TENCORE reports delivering more than 5,000 UGVs to Ukrainian units since 2024; that historical figure is not a new order or delivery commitment under this MoU.

sections.heading: Plans still require execution
paragraphs: The partners intend to add AuraNet onboard and pursue an Arctic-capable version. Definitive agreements remain outstanding, so the announcement does not establish an operating Canadian line, new delivery volumes or test results for the combined system.

dynamic-creatures-hugo-43-actuator-demo-.title: Dynamic Creatures shows Hugo, a character robot with 43 actuators
dynamic-creatures-hugo-43-actuator-demo-.summary: The new video illustrates its hospitality ambitions; unsupervised guest interaction remains unproven.

sections.heading: A mobile guest-facing character
paragraphs: Dynamic Creatures released a Hugo video on October 12, showing a purple furry robot raising a hand and moving through an office. The company describes 43 actuators combined with character design and expressive movement for entertainment and hospitality.

sections.heading: Expression remains in development
paragraphs: Its Vision-Language-Expression model is being developed to connect perception and language with gestures, movement and emotional expression. Navigation and close-contact safety are also described as work in progress, not fully established capabilities.

sections.heading: Autonomy and hardware are unconfirmed
paragraphs: A development-screen image resembles a modified Unitree G1, but the company has not confirmed that identification. Its earlier Boston Dynamics partnership does not identify Hugo’s hardware either. The clip provides no intervention rate or sustained guest-operation results.

robros-korea-20-robot-industrial-sandbox.summary: The sandbox permits testing near workers with risk controls; it is not a completed factory-performance result.

sections.heading: Permission for real-site testing
paragraphs: Seoul Economic Daily reports that South Korea granted Robros a regulatory-sandbox exemption to trial 20 humanoids at manufacturing and logistics sites. This authorizes testing; it does not establish that all robots are deployed or have passed performance tests.

sections.heading: Four industrial settings
paragraphs: The named sites are Nepes, Sungwoo Hitech, HD Hyundai Samho and Delivery Lab. Planned tasks include cleaning semiconductor-packaging components, positioning vehicle body parts, stacking shipbuilding support components and moving refrigerated logistics containers.

sections.heading: Evidence for future safety standards
